generation.forward_push_derivation: For every stance leg, x_body=sign*0.080+stride*(0.5-phase/duty), so dx_body/dt=-stride*cadence/duty. A stationary contact center would therefore imply forward body speed +stride*cadence/duty. Rigid-shoe rolling/sliding can change actual speed.
generation.swing_return: Hermite quintic: -stride/2+tangent*u+(stride-tangent)*smoothstep5(u), tangent=-stride*(1-duty)/duty. Position, velocity and acceleration match constant-speed stance at both joins.

contact_schedule.proof: Contact masks are constant between listed phase events; every open event interval has >=3 scheduled supports.

limitations: No dynamics, balance, policy inference or real hardware validation has been run.
Three scheduled supports do not establish physical contact or COM projection inside the support polygon.
No payload, mass, COM, torque cap, drive gain or motion safety limit is changed by a reference.
Level-body/zero-abduction corner geometry allows <=0.235 mm smoothing clearance; loaded posture can erase lift.
Rigid-shoe contact-edge rolling means matched stance-center velocities do not prove exact no-slip contact.
A packet hold can still activate the unchanged two-degree per-packet cap on recovery.
Startup/stop blending is not covered by periodic geometric rate bounds.
This intentionally slow contact curriculum is not a running gait or a claimed hardware speed.
